model: Series IEFB insertion thermal energy meter, BACnet MS/TP
applies_to: Dwyer Series IEFB insertion electromagnetic flow meters with inlet/outlet RTDs that calculate thermal energy, on BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU.
summary: The IEFB is an insertion electromagnetic flow meter with two RTDs that calculates heating and cooling energy. The RS-485 port runs Modbus RTU by default or BACnet MS/TP, set from the display. Over BACnet it reports velocity and both temperatures as Analog Inputs, and flow, power, energy totals, delta T and year/month peak values as Analog Values, with status bitstrings, peak dates and a few writable setup values.
notes: Units shown are the printed defaults; the Units property of most analog objects is writable, so the site may use other units.
The property tables for AV 9-12 (power peaks) show kilojoules as the default unit; units are left blank here.
The manual prints the AV 8 property table under the AV 7 Cooling Energy heading; the overview table names AV 8 Differential Temperature.
Bit-String Values BSV 1-2 and Date Values DV 1-4 are listed as Other with their printed instances (BSV 1-2, DV 1-4); the description says which object type each is.
The MSV 2 property table repeats the name "Velocity Probe Location"; the overview table names it RTD Locations.

source.title: Series IEFB Insertion Thermal Energy Meter - Specifications, Installation and Operating Instructions

integration.summary: Pick BACnet in the display's communication wizard, set an address 0-127, then read power, the heat and cooling energy totals, flow and both temperatures. Set glycol concentration and process pressure to match the system so the energy maths is right.

minimum_points.name: Empty Pipe
minimum_points.why: Empty pipe (no fluid at the probe)

setup: Protocol, address and serial settings are set from the display; the factory protocol is Modbus RTU.
BACnet addresses run 0-127; the device instance defaults to 607xxx and follows the address until written.
A J1 jumper on the terminal board switches in the 120 ohm termination resistor (default off).
gotchas: Glycol concentration (AV 17) and process pressure (AV 16) feed the energy calculation.
Heat Changeover Temperature (AV 15) decides whether energy counts as heating or cooling.
Writing BV 4 resets all energy totals, peaks, peak dates and the hour counter.
